title: QCDIAG: additional logcode implementations (WCDMA)
description:
Additional logcodes implemented:
- WCDMA Search Cell Reselection Rank (0x4005)
- WCDMA RRC States (0x4125)
- WCDMA RRC Protocol Errors (0x4126)
- WCDMA Cell Id (0x4127)
- WCDMA UL Channel Mapping (0x4128)
- WCDMA RLC DL AM Signaling PDU (0x4135)
- WCDMA RLC UL AM Signaling PDU (0x413C)
- WCDMA RLC UL AM Control PDU (0x4145)
- WCDMA RLC DL AM Control PDU (0x4146)
- WCDMA RLC DL Cipher PDU (0x4168)
- WCDMA RLC UL Cipher PDU (0x4169)
- WCDMA Frequency Scan (0x41B0)

Minor corrections:
- Addressing Coverity Resource leaks issues (element, wmem_strbuf_finalize())

Code improvements:
- New Sources added in the header comment
- WCDMA log code dictionary updates
- hdr tvb functions introduced (e.g. get_gsmtap_hdr_tvb())

Examples: [qcdiag_log.pcapng](/uploads/440deef11584ad36ca5afb2b9d912d6d/qcdiag_log.pcapng), [qcdiag_log_wcdma.pcapng](/uploads/fcbf90907e49dab799aae5a83b78a726/qcdiag_log_wcdma.pcapng)

Additional participants: @laf0rge, @osmith42, @lynxis, @martin.r.mathieson

Saw this:

![image.png](/uploads/78fc0e5a0d65f0a953bc4b5215c37ba0/image.png){width=900 height=439}

I saw that too when I ran Coverity for my code changes but I want to handle this separately, if you don't mind.

`XML_PARSE_NOENT` issue is not specific to QCDIAG, it is an issue for every `xmlReadFile()` which uses this flag anywhere in Wireshark.

`XML_PARSE_NOENT` issue does not impact this MR in general.

I had a quick test and if I remove `XML_PARSE_NOENT` then the XML dictionary is not read in and every log code is Unknown... So for now `XML_PARSE_NOENT` has to be there.

The following files have `XML_PARSE_NOENT` within `xmlReadFile()`:
- epan/dissectors/packet-diameter.c
- epan/dissectors/packet-qcdiag.c
- plugins/epan/wimaxasncp/packet-wimaxasncp.c
- wiretap/nettrace_3gpp_32_423.c

The following files do NOT have `XML_PARSE_NOENT` within `xmlReadFile()`:
- epan/dissectors/json-dictionary.c
- epan/dissectors/packet-knxip_decrypt.c
- plugins/epan/profinet/packet-dcerpc-pn-io.c

I would still suggest to handle this Coverity issue with `XML_PARSE_NOENT` in a separate MR.

Maybe slightly clearer here if this line has an else?

Version value there can be 0, 1, or 2.

hf_qcdiag_wcdma_crr_resel_status shall be added to the tree is version is 1 or above (version is 1 or 2 for now).

hf_qcdiag_wcdma_crr_hcs_priority, hf_qcdiag_wcdma_crr_h_value, hf_qcdiag_wcdma_crr_hcs_cell_qualify shall be added to the tree is version is 2 or above (version is 2 for now).

There reason it's not `version == 2` because if version 3 is added, this would fail.
Ah, I misread the tests, they can both be true.

Couldn't this loop indefinitely if num_gsm is read as 0?

I mean it will throw as soon as it tries to access beyond a TVB, but logically should you check the value and avoid the loop?

`num_gsm` is 0 or a positive integer (`uint8_t`).

if `num_gsm` is 0 then `for (i = 0; i < num_gsm; i++)` is never executed, does not run ("i=0 < 0" -> false). This works as expected.

if `num_gsm` is >0 then `for (i = 0; i < num_gsm; i++)` is executed, from 0 till num_gsm-1.

How could this be an infinite loop?

`for()` handles such cases and no need extra check.

I'd rather you make the precedence clearer, e.g.,

(100 \* mcc1 )+ (10 \* mcc2) + mcc3

or even

100\*mcc1 + 10\*mcc2 + mcc3

changed this line in [version 14 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/23708/diffs?diff_id=1686094260&start_sha=9e84210f49a4b9abe6496fa0709323afebc24265#3f9bf15cbd698a6492dccf1870b37f8bad11b013_1279_1279)

It's from [packet-e212.c](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blame/master/epan/dissectors/packet-e212.c?ref_type=heads#L4109), I simply reused it.

We don’t need the extra brackets because of Operator Precedence: Multiplication, Division and Modulo have higher precedence.

How the compiler sees it:
1. It identifies the \* operators and calculates `100 * mcc1` and `10 * mcc2` first.
2. It then takes those results and performs the + operations from left to right (associativity).

The arithmetic expressions follow the math rules but I can update it for a better visual representation: `100\*mcc1 + 10\*mcc2 + mcc3`
That is clearer to me, thanks.

I think this is ok now - see note about making these arithmetic expressions a little clearer.

You cannot declare the real data on the stack. Allocate this with `pinfo->pool`, like with the other TVBs.

The lifetime of the TVB's data needs to be until the frame has finished processing, and the data can be used (e.g., for tshark to print or the GUI to show in the byte window) after this dissector returns.
Thanks John, you have a valid point. May I fix this with a new MR tomorrow, please?

It's going to be something like this:

`uint8_t *udp_bytes, *arr_ptr;`

`udp_bytes = (uint8_t*)wmem_alloc0(pinfo->pool, 8);`
